newsitem.title: FRANCE: Archaeologists find emperor's statue in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Archaeologists find emperor's statue in Algeria.

text.p: Archaeologists have found a marble statue believed to be of an emperor in northeastern Algeria, near the frontier with Tunisia, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Wednesday.

The statue was found 38 km (23 miles) north of the town of Souk Ahras, a region known for archaeological sites including a 5,000-seat theatre, a statue of Jesus Christ, and an emperor's palace. APS did say what historical era the statue came from.
Many of the remains found in northern Algeria date back to the Roman era.
